headline: Attention architectures encode genomic structure in microbial prediction models
label: Attention Models For Microbial Biology
summary: Explicit set, hierarchical, and cross-modal attention designs are now being applied to bacterial and mycobacterial prediction tasks, all preprint-based.
synthesis: The common thread is explicit architectural encoding of biological structure. GL-HAT applies hierarchical attention over genome-level inputs on a pretrained genomic model, reporting F1 0.845 and AUROC 0.953 for bacterial antimicrobial resistance and identifying resistance-related genomic contexts. VAMP-Net combines permutation-invariant set attention over genomic variant sets with a 1D-CNN on VCF quality metrics for Mycobacterium tuberculosis drug resistance. B-PPI uses cross-attention over ProstT5 embeddings to predict bacterial protein-protein interactions and outperforms TT3D. What is new is set-level, hierarchical, or cross-modal attention built directly into model design. MicroGenomer and the NLP-based phenotype study extend large-scale representation learning to microbial traits, though without the same explicit architectural focus. All results are preprint-based or pending independent validation.
